rounds.proof_sketch: M = matrix.size(1) = 4096 (fixed). Original predicate: 4096 >= 1024 → TRUE. Mutated predicate: 4096 >= 1023 → TRUE. Both evaluate identically. The mutation only distinguishes when M ∈ [1023, 1023], requiring M = 1023 exactly, which violates the fixed-shape contract.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the kernel selection threshold from M >= 1024 to M >= 1023. With the fixed input specification where the matrix B has shape [4096, 4096], the value M = 4096 is immutable. For M = 4096, both conditions evaluate to TRUE, so both original and mutated code execute the identical optimized kernel (diag_matmul_kernel_optimized) with identical grid/block dimensions. The behavioral difference would only manifest when M = 1023 exactly, where the original would use the simple kernel and the mutant would use the optimized kernel. Since shapes cannot be changed per the testing contract, this boundary condition is unreachable.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under the fixed-shape contract. To kill it, one would need M = 1023 (input tensor B with shape [N, 1023]), which violates the constraint that shapes must remain [4096] and [4096, 4096]. No value-level variation within the fixed shapes can trigger the different code path since kernel selection depends solely on the shape dimension M, not on tensor values.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing for GPU kernels should include shape-dependent branch coverage metrics. When kernel dispatch logic depends on tensor dimensions (like the M >= 1024 threshold), test suites should exercise inputs near those thresholds (M = 1023, 1024, 1025). For fixed-shape deployments, consider removing unreachable code paths through compile-time specialization or documenting that certain dimension-based branches are dead code for the deployed configuration.
